domains.description: Forensic financial and operational analysis for property preservation businesses in the United States. Covers cash flow risk, vendor performance, compliance exposure, and portfolio health. Designed for operators, investors, and portfolio reviewers who need data-backed insight, not summaries.

reports.title: Financial Health: The Cash Chain
reports.executive_summary: Analysis of receivables, vendor payment cycles, and work order volume trends reveals a pattern of cash flow compression common to mid-sized property preservation operators.
key_findings: Less than half of invoiced revenue is realized as collected cash.
Receivable concentration creates a single-client liquidity risk.
Collections have collapsed while contractor payments remain active.
reports.methodology_note: Analysis is based on 268 work order records spanning May to December 2025, using operator-provided accounting ledgers and client validation portal logs.
reports.dataset_reference: Operator accounting ledgers and validation portal logs

reports.title: Leakage Breakdown: Structural Autopsy
reports.executive_summary: Forensic audit of margin erosion mapping total leakage by vendor, cause, and client, isolating contractor cost overruns as the dominant loss category.
key_findings: Contractor overruns represent the dominant leakage pattern.
Leakage clusters by client and validation pathway.
Margin erosion is structural rather than incidental.
reports.methodology_note: Analysis groups leakage by vendor, client, and work order classification using the supplied operating ledger.
reports.dataset_reference: Operator work order and payment ledger

reports.title: Work Order Breakdown: The Risk Matrix
reports.executive_summary: Quantitative review ranking service categories by leakage and income efficiency, exposing high-volume loss-making activities.
key_findings: High-volume service lines can still destroy cash when validation friction is high.
Some low-frequency work types carry disproportionate leakage risk.
Service categories should be repriced, monitored, or scaled based on efficiency.
reports.methodology_note: Analysis ranks 13 service categories by income ratio, leakage rate, and work order volume.
reports.dataset_reference: Service-level work order and payment data

reports.title: Interactive Workbook & Dashboard
reports.executive_summary: Interactive Looker Studio dashboard and Google Sheets workbook built directly on 268 forensic work order records to automate tracking of margin erosion, aging receivables, and contractor efficiency.
key_findings: Integrates live data pipelines to visual dashboards.
Allows filtering by client, region (ZIP), contractor, and service lines.
Click-to-inspect formulas for full calculation auditing.
reports.methodology_note: Built using standard spreadsheets formulas (SUMIFS, VLOOKUP, IFERROR) and Looker Studio widgets.
